page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8i.xlarge is a general-purpose compute instance built on the KVM virtualization layer and x86_64 architecture. Hardware resources are powered by an Intel Xeon 8475B processor running at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz across 4 dedicated vCPUs. The instance features 16.0 GB of memory, establishing a 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB allocated per virtual core.

In terms of I/O and storage architecture, ecs.g8i.xlarge includes no integrated local storage, requiring persistent operational workloads to rely on remote block storage solutions. The instance is provisioned with a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Discrete GPU hardware is absent from this configuration, concentrating system resources entirely on general host processing and standard network operations.

The instance provides dedicated processor execution, avoiding resource contention typical of burstable platforms. Because CPU and memory are balanced in a standard enterprise proportion, ecs.g8i.xlarge is aligned with intermediate web application hosting, mid-sized relational database management systems, microservices runtimes, and continuous integration pipelines that require predictable compute throughput without demanding specialized hardware accelerators.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8i.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon 8475B processor clocked at 2.7 GHz, coupled with 16.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The server does not bundle local disk storage, necessitating external network-attached volumes for persistent data, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With zero discrete GPUs, this configuration delivers steady dedicated compute capacity suitable for applications requiring consistent multi-core performance without hardware acceleration. The resource profile supports balanced computing workloads including mid-tier web serving, application backends, container hosting, lightweight relational database deployments, and continuous integration services.
